expectations.text: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
expectations.evidence: The spec includes `Clarifications, Assumptions, And Recorded Questions`; the companion notes file also records questions and assumptions.

expectations.text: Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: The spec includes summary, existing context, clarifications, scope, non-goals, proposed convention, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification plan, risks, and open questions.

expectations.text: Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
expectations.evidence: Requirements use `MEM-REQ-###`, acceptance criteria use `MEM-AC-###`, and memory entries use `MEM-YYYYMMDD-NNN`.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
expectations.evidence: Acceptance criteria include file existence, heading inspection, regex checks for IDs, line-count checks, and source-field inspection.

expectations.text: Mentions relevant existing workspace context such as current skills, docs, or instruction files based on read-only inspection.
expectations.evidence: The existing workspace context section references `engineering-context`, `session-retrospective`, and `ticket-workflow` skills and the absence of root instruction files.

expectations.text: Converts a broad idea into one focused spec rather than producing a broad documentation rewrite or downstream ticket set.
expectations.evidence: The spec focuses on a single `.context/agent-memory.md` convention and explicitly excludes tickets, implementation code, and broad documentation rewrites.

uncertainties: Timing/token metrics were not available in the completion notifications.
